text:
maya: Quick async check — hitting a weird edge when `stop` sequences + `max_tokens` small + `logprobs` requested. stop seems ignored and we get truncated token but still return logprobs for partial token. Anyone seen this?

alex: can you paste a minimal repro? curl or python snippet is fine.

maya: repro below (can paste more if helpful):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"open-llama-7b","input":"Finish: Hello","max_tokens":3,"temperature":0.0,"top_p":1.0,"stop":["\n"],"logprobs":5}'
```
sample response we saw:
```json
{
  "id":"gen_123","object":"generation","choices":[{
    "text":"Hello world\n","logprobs":{...},
    "finish_reason":"max_tokens"
  }]
}
```
Note: `\n` is in `stop` but finish_reason is `max_tokens` and newline still appears. Also logprobs include probs for trailing newline token that ideally should have been suppressed.

sarah: hmm two things: 1) our runtime stops generation when `max_tokens` boundary is hit (hard cap). 2) `stop` is a post-generation check in streaming mode: it triggers early stop only when stop sequence is recognized exactly in token stream, otherwise it may be detected after tokenization boundaries. With tiny `max_tokens` you can have tokenizer emit pieces that include stop chars but not match full sequence -> we return the produced token and label finish_reason=max_tokens.

li: additional nuance: when `logprobs` requested we compute token-level probs for emitted tokens. If a stop would have removed a suffix post-tokenization, logprobs for the emitted token remain because they correspond to the raw token output.

chris: TL;DR: behavior is consistent with current contract but is surprising. We probably need to document the precedence and tokenization caveat and decide if we want to change runtime to attempt stop-matching at sub-token granularity (expensive).

maya: thanks. For customers hitting this it's confusing. Would a small compatibility shim be acceptable — e.g., prefer `stop` over `max_tokens` when `stop` is unambiguous byte-sequence at token boundary?

alex: options:
- keep current (fast) and document explicitly (low risk)
- attempt multi-step lookahead to drop trailing partial tokens if they contain stop suffix (medium risk)
- post-filter output text and remove stop sequences (simple) but then what to do with logprobs/finish_reason? (we'd have to set finish_reason="stop" and strip tokens which would make logprobs inconsistent)

maya: product question: which behavior do we promise in the API contract? @sarah any preference?

sarah: product prefers predictable semantics. I think we should: 1) document that `max_tokens` is a hard cap; 2) document that `stop` is applied at token boundaries and may not override a prior hard cap; 3) add an optional param `apply_stop_post_filter=true|false` that when true will post-filter returned text to remove stop sequences and set finish_reason to `stop` but will NOT adjust logprobs (we'll also warn about mismatch). Default false to preserve backward compatibility.

li: engineering notes: adding `apply_stop_post_filter` is cheap at API layer. We must add tests to ensure streaming clients unaffected. Also need to update SDKs to expose new flag.

chris: and we should add unit tests covering interplay: (a) stop breaks at token boundary, (b) stop across tokenization boundary with small max_tokens, (c) request with `logprobs`.

maya: PR incoming: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/678 — adds param + docs + tests. pinging reviewers. @alex @li please review when you have a sec.

alex: will review today, quick skim looks fine. One note: docs must include example for deterministic tests (use `temperature:0` + `seed` if available).

deploy-bot: canary deployed runtime patch `feat/stop-postfilter` to `canary-3` at 2024-05-10T18:12:05Z :rocket: (watching metrics).

maya: excellent. Follow-ups: I'll update API contract doc in docs/api/generate.md to include the new param and explicit precedence matrix. Also adding an open test in `eng-ml/tests` to capture regression.

sarah: thanks — schedule a short sync if anyone thinks we should change default. otherwise ship doc + flag.

li: adding test vectors now.

chris: resolved for now. marking as async-ack. :white_check_mark:

maya: thanks all — closing the loop here. If customers escalate, we'll consider runtime-level match-on-subtoken research.
